papers.title: Millisecond-Scale Calibration and Benchmarking of Superconducting Qubits
papers.authors: Malthe A. Marciniak, Rune T. Birke, Johann B. Severin, Fabrizio Berritta, Daniel Kjær, Filip Nilsson, Smitha N. Themadath, Sangeeth Kallatt, James L. Webb, Kristoffer Bentsen, Tonny Madsen, Zhenhai Sun, Svend Krøjer, Christopher W. Warren, Jacob Hastrup, Morten Kjaergaard

papers.title: Perspective: Reproducible Coherence Characterization of Superconducting Quantum Devices
papers.authors: Corey Rae H. McRae, Gregory M. Stiehl, Haozhi Wang, Sheng-Xiang Lin, Shane A. Caldwell, David P. Pappas, Josh Mutus, Joshua Combes
papers.what_it_establishes: Argues that coherence metrics as currently reported cannot be validly compared across measurements, devices and laboratories, and proposes best practices and order-of-magnitude expectations for variation of qubit and resonator performance metrics.
papers.overlap_reason: Community-standards precedent for the material's implicit argument that published specifications are insufficient for prediction. Concerns cross-lab comparability of coherence metrics rather than cross-session reproducibility of a circuit result.

papers.title: Not All Qubits Are Created Equal: A Case for Variability-Aware Policies for NISQ-Era Quantum Computers
papers.authors: Swamit S. Tannu, Moinuddin K. Qureshi
papers.what_it_establishes: Quantifies variation in qubit and link error rates from IBM-Q20 characterization data and proposes variation-aware qubit movement and allocation, improving reliability up to 1.9x on IBM-Q5.
papers.overlap_reason: Foundational for spatial (qubit-to-qubit) variation and the practice of reading vendor calibration reports as a time series; the material's register non-monotonicity touches the spatial half of this. Predominantly spatial, not a session-to-session stability study.

papers.title: Quantum Computing in the Cloud: Analyzing job and machine characteristics
papers.authors: Gokul Subramanian Ravi, Kaitlin N. Smith, Pranav Gokhale, Frederic T. Chong
papers.venue_year: IEEE International Symposium on Workload Characterization (IISWC) 2021, pp. 39-50
papers.identifier: IISWC 2021 (NSF PAR record 10313645); no arXiv id confirmed
papers.what_it_establishes: Characterizes cloud quantum computing job and machine behaviour, including resource consumption and execution characteristics relevant to job/resource management.
papers.overlap_reason: Listed because it is the standard citation for empirical characterization of cloud quantum access, which is the delivery model the material is stress-testing. I could NOT verify whether it contains temporal-variation analysis of device properties — I only saw the venue record and a one-line abstract snippet. Do not cite it for a drift claim without reading it.

papers.title: Stability studies on subtractively-fabricated CMOS-compatible superconducting transmon qubits
papers.authors: Not verified (arXiv listing not fetched in full; a D. Zahn appears among the authors per an arXiv author-search hit)
papers.what_it_establishes: Tracks two representative transmons across 10 cooldown cycles spanning more than one year, and monitors T1/T2* over a 95-hour single cooldown, attributing fluctuations primarily to TLS-qubit interaction. A search snippet reported ~3.4% average variation over 400 days, which I could not confirm against the paper text.
papers.overlap_reason: Longest-baseline stability characterization I found for superconducting transmons, relevant as the fabrication-side counterpoint to the material's session-scale swings. Author list and the 3.4%/400-day figure are unverified — do not cite either without checking the paper.

papers.title: Certified Finite-Shot Operating Windows for Virtual Distillation and Symmetry Verification
papers.authors: Vicenzo Scavino Alfaro
papers.venue_year: arXiv preprint, quant-ph; v1 13 June 2026, v2 21 June 2026
papers.what_it_establishes: Finite-shot comparison of virtual distillation and symmetry verification with a 'pre-specified analysis' reporting 300/300 sign agreement, tested against archived IBM hardware runs, and transparently reporting that 'the single strict all-instance criterion not met is reported with its calibration analysis'.
papers.overlap_reason: Same emerging practice family as the material (pre-specified criteria, all-instance reporting, explicit reporting of the one criterion that fails), but the analysis is pre-specified rather than pre-registered before data existed, hardware is archived rather than prospectively submitted, and the subject is error-mitigation operating windows, not device-specification adequacy.

papers.title: Microstructural Topology as a Prescriptor for Quantum Coherence: Towards A Unified Framework for Decoherence in Superconducting Qubits
papers.authors: Vinayak P. Dravid, Akshay A. Murthy, Peter Lim, Gabriel T. dos Santos, Ramandeep Mandia, James M. Rondinelli, Mark C. Hersam, Roberto dos Reis
papers.venue_year: arXiv preprint, quant-ph; v1 5 Apr 2026, v2 12 Apr 2026
papers.what_it_establishes: A separable framework for transmon decoherence in which 'Falsifiability is operationalized through a pre-committed 2x2 experimental protocol in which the variables must satisfy independent ratio checks within propagated uncertainty', plus a Minimum-Dataset Specification standardizing cross-laboratory reporting. Part I is conceptual and mathematical only; coordinated experimental validation is explicitly reserved for Part II.
papers.overlap_reason: Shows pre-commitment language entering mainstream superconducting-qubit physics from a well-known materials group, which is useful precedent for the material's framing. But no hardware was run, no prediction was measured, and no outcome is reported, so it cannot pre-empt a completed pre-registered measurement study.

papers.title: Validation of an Analysability Model in Hybrid Quantum Software
papers.authors: Ana Díaz-Muñoz, José A. Cruz-Lemus, Moisés Rodríguez, Mario Piattini, Maria Teresa Baldassarre
papers.what_it_establishes: An explicit 'registered report proposal' in a quantum context: a controlled experiment with human subjects across Italian and Spanish institutions to validate an analysability quality model for hybrid quantum-classical software.
papers.overlap_reason: The only registered report I found touching quantum computing at all, and it arrives via software engineering, where registered reports are an established format - not via physics. It concerns human comprehension of code, not quantum hardware measurement. Useful as evidence that the format reaches quantum research only through its computer-science border.

papers.title: Blind Analysis in Nuclear and Particle Physics
papers.authors: Joshua R. Klein, Aaron Roodman
papers.venue_year: Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science 55, 141-163 (2005)
papers.what_it_establishes: The canonical statement of physics's own answer to experimenter bias. Blind analysis prevents experimenters from knowing the answer until the analysis is complete; the review argues there is at least circumstantial evidence that bias has affected past measurements, and that as experiments grow costlier and harder to reproduce, the risk grows. Catalogues the practical blinding schemes in use.
papers.overlap_reason: Establishes the norms baseline the material must position against. Blinding and pre-registration are different instruments: blinding hides the answer so analysis choices cannot be tuned toward it; pre-registration fixes the claim so it cannot be revised after the answer is seen. The material does the latter. Physics has a strong institutional tradition of the former in particle, nuclear and dark-matter physics, and essentially none of either in quantum computing.

papers.title: Blind Analysis in Particle Physics
papers.authors: Aaron Roodman
papers.what_it_establishes: Reviews the blind-analysis technique, its historical development, the danger of experimenter bias, three distinct types of blind analysis, and BABAR's implementation.
papers.overlap_reason: Supporting norms citation alongside Klein and Roodman; documents that the discipline's bias-control vocabulary is 'blinding', not 'pre-registration'.

papers.title: Blind analysis in Physics experiments: Is this trip necessary?
papers.authors: Robert Golub
papers.what_it_establishes: An explicitly dissenting note: building on Klein and Roodman, it presents an alternate conclusion about the value of blind analysis in physics experiments. I verified the title, author, date and the one-sentence abstract; I did NOT read the full argument, so I can characterise the position only as skeptical.
papers.overlap_reason: Relevant because it shows the norms question is contested inside physics, not settled. A referee sympathetic to this view will ask the material to justify why pre-commitment was worth the cost; the material's answer (a >17 SE miss that would otherwise have been quietly re-derived) is a strong empirical reply and should be framed as one.

papers.title: Blinding multi-probe cosmological experiments
papers.authors: J. Muir, G. M. Bernstein, D. Huterer, et al. (Dark Energy Survey Collaboration)
papers.venue_year: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society; arXiv v1 13 Nov 2019, revised 4 May 2020
papers.what_it_establishes: Method for concealing inferred cosmological parameters until all analysis decisions are final, by shifting summary statistics while preserving internal-consistency checks; demonstrated on simulated DES clustering and lensing data. Motivated explicitly by preventing scientists from biasing analysis toward theoretically expected results, especially when new results are scrutinized for consistency with previous ones.
papers.overlap_reason: Second pillar of the physics norms baseline: cosmology institutionalized blinding, and did so precisely because results get judged against prior expectations. Establishes that when a physics subfield decides analyst bias is a live threat, it reaches for blinding rather than pre-registration - which is what makes the material's choice a methodological argument that needs making.

papers.title: A blinding solution for inference from astronomical data
papers.authors: Elena Sellentin
papers.venue_year: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society (2020); arXiv 18 October 2019
papers.what_it_establishes: A joint blinding/deblinding strategy allowing up to three blinding stages - data, theory computation, and covariance matrix - applied to KiDS-450 weak lensing. Shows covariance blinding is especially effective, and that undetected covariance errors can bias conclusions in ways that mimic real tension.
papers.overlap_reason: Norms citation. Its substantive point is also thematically close to the material: an error in an unmodelled part of the uncertainty budget can masquerade as a physical discrepancy - the material's readout-specification gap is the hardware analogue.

papers.title: The preregistration revolution
papers.authors: Brian A. Nosek, Charles R. Ebersole, Alexander C. DeHaven, David T. Mellor
papers.venue_year: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA 115(11), 2600-2606 (2018)
papers.what_it_establishes: The standard reference defining pre-registration, its purpose (separating confirmatory from exploratory inference, blocking HARKing and undisclosed analytic flexibility), and the case for adoption across the sciences.
papers.overlap_reason: Definitional citation the material needs, since its audience will not know the term as a term of art. No quantum or physical-science content.

papers.title: The preregistration revolution needs to distinguish between predictions and analyses
papers.authors: Alison Ledgerwood
papers.venue_year: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA (2018), letter
papers.what_it_establishes: Argues that pre-registering a prediction and pre-registering an analysis plan are different acts with different epistemic force; Nosek et al. replied under the title 'Predictions without analysis plans are inert'.
papers.overlap_reason: Directly germane to how the material should describe itself. The material locked numeric point predictions (0.8932 purity, 1.500 anchor) to version control. Referees who know this literature will ask whether the analysis pipeline was locked too, or only the numbers. The material should state which, because this exchange is the standard place that question comes from.

papers.title: Preregistration for Experiments with AI Agents
papers.authors: Michelle Vaccaro
papers.what_it_establishes: A position paper cataloguing researcher degrees of freedom specific to a new computational experimental field and proposing a field-specific pre-registration template.
papers.overlap_reason: No quantum content. Included as the structural precedent for what a 'pre-registration for quantum hardware experiments' contribution looks like as a paper: enumerate the degrees of freedom the platform creates, then propose the template. If the material wants a methodological contribution rather than only a physics result, this is the model, and it shows the slot is filled in AI and empty in quantum.

papers.title: Wire-Level Interrupt-to-Decision Latency of On-Sensor MLC versus Host Inference on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano: A Pre-Registered Measurement Study
papers.authors: Swami, Sonawane (full given names not verified)
papers.what_it_establishes: A hardware measurement study carried out under an explicit pre-registration, with the pre-registration recorded as a README commit (commit 9c738a8, 2026-04-16) and a separate pilot-and-verdict commit two days later.
papers.overlap_reason: Not quantum, and not physics. Included for one specific reason: it is direct precedent for the exact mechanism the material uses - a git commit as the pre-registration timestamp for a hardware measurement study - so the material cannot claim that mechanism as novel, only its application to quantum hardware. Verified from search-result text quoting the commit hash and dates, not from the PDF itself.

papers.title: Scalable mitigation of measurement errors on quantum computers
papers.authors: Paul D. Nation, Hwajung Kang, Neereja Sundaresan, Jay M. Gambetta
papers.what_it_establishes: The M3 matrix-free mitigation method, working in the subspace of observed bitstrings and accommodating both uncorrelated and correlated errors; a correlated-M3 variant is reported to agree with the full assignment matrix, and Hamming-distance truncation is used to approximate the mitigation.
papers.overlap_reason: Standard tooling context, and its Hamming-distance truncation is the closest existing use of an excitation-weight-like structure in readout mitigation. It is a mitigation method, not a characterisation of the physical weight dependence, so it does not scoop the saturation claim.

papers.title: Crosstalk In Contemporary Quantum Devices
papers.authors: Spiro Gicev, Ben Harper, Haiyue Kang, Muhammad Usman, Martin Sevior
papers.what_it_establishes: A 2026 cross-platform review of crosstalk covering physical origins, mitigation and security implications. Its readout-crosstalk section notes that the state of adjacent qubits can affect a readout result in frequency-multiplexed superconducting systems, and focuses on machine-learning discrimination as the mitigation route.
papers.overlap_reason: Most valuable as NEGATIVE evidence for the novelty argument: the field's most recent survey, three months old, does not report saturation of readout crosstalk with excitation weight and does not raise vendor omission of readout error. Verified by fetching the HTML of v2 and asking directly about both points.

papers.title: Measurement-induced state transitions in multi-qubit transmon processors
papers.authors: Baptiste Hoyau, Alexander McDonald, Boris M. Varbanov, Manuel H. Munoz-Arias, Alexandre Blais
papers.what_it_establishes: Theory/characterisation of measurement-induced state transitions (MIST) when a transmon couples to other circuit elements. Reports that a spectator qubit can be affected by the measurement-induced transition of the qubit being read out, and conversely that the presence of a spectator LOWERS the MIST threshold of the read-out qubit.
papers.overlap_reason: Supplies a candidate physical mechanism for excitation-dependent readout error that is not simple resonator-tone leakage, and the reciprocal spectator effect is the kind of nonlinearity that could produce saturation. Relevant to the material's 'seven candidate mechanisms bounded or excluded' section; two transmons plus a coupler, not a device-scale study.

papers.title: Transmon qubit readout fidelity at the threshold for quantum error correction without a quantum-limited amplifier
papers.authors: Liangyu Chen, Hang-Xi Li, Yong Lu, Christopher W. Warren, Christian J. Krizan, Sandoko Kosen, Marcus Rommel, Shahnawaz Ahmed, Amr Osman, Janka Biznarova, Anita Fadavi Roudsari, Benjamin Lienhard, Marco Caputo, Kestutis Grigoras, Leif Groenberg, Joonas Govenius, Anton Frisk Kockum, Per Delsing, Jonas Bylander, Giovanna Tancredi
papers.what_it_establishes: Reports 99.5% two-state and 96.9% three-state assignment fidelity, and is the standard reference for readout physics in transmons -- relaxation during readout as the dominant error, and fidelity loss when readout drive amplitude excites higher levels.
papers.overlap_reason: Background for the material's asymmetry-in-the-T1-direction observation. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: search snippets circulating numbers of 97.3% (global ground state) versus 91.3% (global excited state) across 16 basis states could NOT be traced to this paper -- the abstract page does not contain them. Do not cite those figures to this reference without reading the full text.

papers.title: Evaluating Calibration-Based Digital Twins for IBM Quantum Hardware Simulation
papers.authors: Edgars Bautra, Maksims Dimitrijevs, Abuzer Yakaryilmaz
papers.what_it_establishes: Builds noise models ('digital twins') from vendor-published calibration CSVs, including per-qubit readout assignment error, and compares them against real execution on ibm_brisbane and ibm_sherbrooke. Readout error enters only as independent per-qubit ReadoutError instances.
papers.overlap_reason: The nearest published instance of the material's 'prediction from published spec vs measured hardware' comparison. It does NOT decompose the residual gap by error source, does not identify readout as dominant, and does not consider correlated readout error -- so the material's reconciliation (0.89 -> 0.75 -> 0.7163 vs 0.7184 measured) is not pre-empted.

papers.title: Few-Shot Cross-Device Transfer for Quantum Noise Modeling on Real Hardware
papers.authors: Sahil Al Farib, Sheikh Redwanul Islam, Azizur Rahman Anik
papers.venue_year: arXiv:2604.24397, 27 April 2026; 9 pages, 8 figures, 8 tables; submitted to IEEE QCE 2026
papers.what_it_establishes: CITED WORK #3 (the 2026 few-shot paper). Trains a residual neural network to map noisy circuit output distributions to ideal ones on a source device and transfers it to a target device with few samples. Devices: ibm_fez (source) -> ibm_marrakesh (target). Dataset: 85 circuits per device, 170 paired samples total; 2-5 qubits, depth 2-8; four families (40 random, 15 Bell, 15 GHZ, 15 QFT); 8,192 shots per circuit. Results: zero-shot transfer KL divergence 1.6706; with 20 fine-tuning samples 1.1924, a 28.6% improvement, recovering 34.9% of the gap to in-domain performance. CX gate error is identified as the dominant cross-device mismatch, readout error second. CRITICALLY FOR OUR PURPOSES, its inputs and its stated limitations run the opposite way from the material: device features are pulled from IBM Quantum's CALIBRATION API at execution time rather than measured independently, features are mean-aggregated rather than per-qubit, and the authors state plainly that they 'do not control for temporal drift between backend executions' while noting that 'IBM Quantum calibration data drifts substantially over hours to days.' No predictions were pre-registered; the study is post-hoc. Five limitations are conceded: small dataset (170 samples, two devices), shallow circuits, mean-aggregated features, no drift modeling, and a simple architecture without classical baselines.
papers.overlap_reason: Same era, same platform family, opposite methodology and opposite conclusion structure. It treats vendor calibration as the trusted feature vector and learns a correction on top; the material treats vendor calibration as the untested hypothesis and finds it off by 3x in the one parameter the spec omits. It explicitly declines to control temporal drift, which is precisely the axis on which the material's largest effect lives (cross-session 0.2 in purity). It is a useful FOIL rather than a competitor: it demonstrates that the 2026 state of practice both depends on vendor readout numbers and knows it has not validated them. The material would add the missing validation, and would supply the drift control the paper lists as future work. There is no claim collision.

papers.title: Mitigating measurement errors in multi-qubit experiments
papers.authors: Sergey Bravyi, Sarah Sheldon, Abhinav Kandala, David C. McKay, Jay M. Gambetta
papers.what_it_establishes: Two measurement-error mitigation schemes by classical post-processing, based on a tensor-product noise model and on a correlated Continuous Time Markov Process (CTMP) model, with error rates extractable from calibration data by a simple formula. The CTMP model explicitly targets crosstalk arising from qubit-qubit coupling and spectral overlap of readout resonators. Demonstrated for measurements of up to 20 qubits.
papers.overlap_reason: The canonical correlated-readout mitigation reference and the standard baseline any reviewer will expect. It establishes that correlated readout is modelled and correctable in principle, which means the material should not claim novelty for the existence of correlated readout. It is a mitigation method paper on IBM hardware, not a measurement of how the correlation scales with the number of excited neighbours, and not an audit of vendor disclosure.

papers.title: Detecting and tracking drift in quantum information processors
papers.authors: Timothy Proctor, Melissa Revelle, Erik Nielsen, et al.
papers.what_it_establishes: A fast, statistically sound spectral-analysis technique for resolving time dependence in quantum processor data, applicable to time-series from any quantum processor experiment. Demonstrates that the widely used characterization tools assume static error modes and rates, which causes unheralded failures, misidentified error modes and wasted experimental effort. Validated on simulations and trapped-ion experiments, and shown to resolve time dependence within randomized benchmarking, gate set tomography and Ramsey spectroscopy.
papers.overlap_reason: The foundational reference establishing that quantum-processor errors are non-stationary and that standard characterization silently assumes otherwise, so it forecloses any claim that instability itself is a new observation. It is a methods paper on detecting drift in time-series, mostly on trapped ions, and it says nothing about vendor specification completeness, readout crosstalk versus excitation weight, or register-size non-monotonicity. Cite as background, not as competition.

papers.title: Computational references are not experiments: pre-registered validation of machine-learned sodium-cathode voltages
papers.authors: Krishna Teja Vepa
papers.what_it_establishes: Not a quantum paper, included as the clearest methodological precedent for the material's protocol. Commits verdict thresholds, failure modes and primary metrics to version control BEFORE analysis, then tests machine-learned cathode voltages against experimental literature values (n=6 after documented exclusion). Finds MAE 0.67 V, a conservative 95% bound of 1.09 V, strongly voltage-dependent residuals (r = -0.94), and that the computational reference database itself carries roughly 0.54 V of systematic error, dominating accuracy more than the model does. Outcome: the screening approach was retired and a follow-up calibration audit pre-registered.
papers.overlap_reason: Structurally the same argument in a different science: predictions frozen in version control before the data existed, a documented miss, and the miss traced to a systematic error in the REFERENCE rather than in the model. That is precisely the shape of the material's finding, where the wrong input is the parameter the specification does not publish. Useful as a citation for the pre-registration protocol and for the 'the reference is the problem' framing. Zero subject-matter overlap; it cannot contest any physics claim.

papers.title: JigSaw: Boosting Fidelity of NISQ Programs via Measurement Subsetting
papers.authors: Poulami Das, Swamit Tannu, Moinuddin Qureshi
papers.what_it_establishes: Shows that measuring a SUBSET of qubits yields lower measurement error than measuring all qubits, because it reduces measurement crosstalk, and exploits the more accurate local distributions to improve the full-register result. Related reported evidence in this line: measurement error rates rise by up to 2% when five qubits are measured simultaneously versus a single qubit in isolation.
papers.overlap_reason: Bears directly on the material's non-monotonicity finding as a COMPETING MECHANISM that must be addressed, and it happens to push the opposite way: measurement crosstalk grows with the number of qubits measured, so it predicts the smaller n=3 register should do BETTER, not worse. That makes it evidence FOR the material's claim that the observed ordering flip (n=3 worse than n=4 despite the n=4 register containing the n=3 one) is not explained by measurement crosstalk. It should be cited in the mechanism-elimination section rather than as prior art on the phenomenon.

papers.title: Isolating Recurring Execution-Dependent Abnormal Patterns on NISQ Quantum Devices
papers.authors: Zhenyu Qi et al. (full author list not verified)
papers.what_it_establishes: A delta-debugging framework showing that 'semantically equivalent circuits with identical compiler-visible costs can still produce unexpected hardware noise.' Identifies 25 recurring abnormal gate patterns, short ordered gate sequences on specific qubit neighbourhoods that induce excess error beyond current noise models. Three IBM Heron r2 backends across 30 qubit layouts (ibm_fez, ibm_marrakesh named), validated ACROSS CALIBRATION WINDOWS so that patterns are recurring rather than one-off. Compares real-device error against calibration-based error from the standard noise model, focusing on the discrepancy. Reports 24% and 45% noise reduction on the two backends.
papers.overlap_reason: Same core move as the material at the methodological level: take the discrepancy between the calibration-based model prediction and the real device as the object of study, and show the standard noise model omits something structural. Its omission is gate-sequence-and-layout dependent excess error on IBM Heron; the material's is readout magnitude, excitation-weight-dependent readout correlation, and cross-session non-stationarity on Rigetti via a broker. Its cross-calibration-window validation is a good precedent for the material's cross-session protocol.

papers.title: Decoherence benchmarking of superconducting qubits
papers.authors: J. Burnett, A. Bengtsson, M. Scigliuzzo, D. Niepce, M. Kudra, P. Delsing, J. Bylander
papers.what_it_establishes: SEED. Multi-day statistics on transmon T1/T2*; mean T1=49us, T2*=95us, both fluctuating enough to force frequent recalibration. Attributes T1 fluctuation to instabilities of near-resonant two-level systems (TLS), local to each qubit; extracts TLS switching rates; capacitance noise sets a 0.8 ms pure-dephasing limit.
papers.overlap_reason: Supplies the accepted microscopic mechanism (TLS reconfiguration) for why a device's coherence is not the same thing two days running. That is the physical licence for the material's cross-session drift finding. But it benchmarks decoherence parameters in a lab-controlled cryostat, not application-level observables (purity), not readout, not cloud access, and never re-runs byte-identical circuits to test outcome reproducibility. No pre-registration.

papers.title: Fluctuations of Energy-Relaxation Times in Superconducting Qubits
papers.authors: P. V. Klimov, J. Kelly, Z. Chen, M. Neeley, et al. (Google)
papers.what_it_establishes: CITED BY SEED. T1 in transmons fluctuates strongly over hours-to-days as TLS drift through the qubit frequency; the fluctuation is large enough to invalidate a single calibration snapshot.
papers.overlap_reason: Establishes that a published median fidelity is a distribution parameter, not a device property -- which is the premise the material's ~0.2-in-purity cross-session swing exploits. It does not measure application-level reproducibility, readout, or purity, and gives no within-session vs cross-session ratio.

papers.title: Correlating Decoherence in Transmon Qubits: Low Frequency Noise by Single Fluctuators
papers.authors: S. Schloer, J. Lisenfeld, C. Mueller, A. Bilmes, et al.
papers.what_it_establishes: CITED BY SEED (concurrent). Correlated decoherence across transmons traced to individual low-frequency fluctuators; qubit parameters wander together on long timescales.
papers.overlap_reason: Nearest published mechanism for a register-scale, spatially structured change between sessions -- relevant to the n=3/n=4 ordering flip, which single-qubit-independent noise cannot produce. It is a spectroscopic study of fluctuators, not a claim about nested-register non-monotonicity, and it does not exclude gate count or readout as the material does.

papers.title: Signal Crosstalk in a Flip-Chip Quantum Processor
papers.authors: S. Kosen, H.-X. Li, M. Rommel, R. Rehammar, et al.
papers.what_it_establishes: Systematic measurement of control-signal crosstalk (capacitive qubit-drive and inductive flux-drive) in a flip-chip architecture, with distance dependence and projected gate-error impact for scaled processors.
papers.overlap_reason: Crosstalk of a different kind -- control/drive, not measurement. Useful only as the counterpart citation establishing that crosstalk is routinely characterized in vendor-side device papers while being absent from the customer-facing specification the material was given. No readout crosstalk, no neighbour-state dependence, no saturation.

papers.title: Detection of temporal fluctuation in superconducting qubits for quantum error mitigation
papers.authors: Y. Hirasaki, S. Daimon, T. Itoko, N. Kanazawa, E. Saitoh
papers.what_it_establishes: Continuous monitoring reveals step-like changes in qubit error rates recurring on a several-minute persistence timescale; demonstrates post-selection error mitigation by correlating elevated error with anomalous output variance.
papers.overlap_reason: Bounds the within-session timescale: minutes-scale telegraphic steps. Consistent with the material's ~1% per-qubit within-session drift and helps argue that the ~0.2 cross-session swing is a different regime, not the same process integrated longer. Post-selection mitigation, not prediction; no purity, no cross-session comparison.

papers.title: Performance Stabilization of High-Coherence Superconducting Qubits
papers.authors: A. Dane, K. Balakrishnan, B. Wacaser, L.-W. Hung, H. J. Mamin, D. Rugar, R. M. Shelby, C. Murray, K. Rodbell, J. Sleight
papers.what_it_establishes: Transmons with T1 > 2.5 ms show variation large enough that fabrication processes cannot be reliably compared; applying a slowly varying electric field to nearby TLS stabilizes measured T1, replacing hundreds of hours of measurement with minutes.
papers.overlap_reason: Reinforces that a single reported coherence number is not a comparable device property without stabilization -- supporting context for why a published median fidelity failed to predict the material's outcome. Vendor-side intervention on the physics; nothing on cloud access, readout, application observables, or session-to-session outcome reproducibility. The abstract does not discuss cross-cooldown variation.

papers.title: Parallel tomography of quantum non-demolition measurements in multi-qubit devices
papers.authors: L. Pereira, Juan José García-Ripoll, Tomás Ramos
papers.what_it_establishes: A parallel tomography protocol for single- and two-qubit readout on a multi-qubit processor, demonstrated on a 7-qubit IBM-Q device. Reconstructs Choi matrices of the measurement processes, extracts fidelity, QNDness and destructiveness, identifies error sources limiting repeated QND measurement, and explicitly shows how to QUANTIFY MEASUREMENT CROSSTALK and use it to certify the quality of simultaneous readout on multiple qubits.
papers.overlap_reason: Establishes that measurement crosstalk on a multiqubit cloud device is a quantifiable, certifiable quantity with a standard protocol. Relevant as the methodological benchmark the material's crosstalk measurement should be positioned against — a referee may ask why overlapping/parallel detector tomography was not used. No overlap on purity, pre-registration, drift, or specification mismatch.

papers.title: Fast Fingerprinting of Cloud-based NISQ Quantum Computers
papers.authors: Kaitlin N. Smith, Joshua Viszlai, Lennart Maximilian Seifert, Jonathan M. Baker, Jakub Szefer, Frederic T. Chong
papers.venue_year: IEEE International Symposium on Hardware Oriented Security and Trust (HOST) 2023
papers.what_it_establishes: Studies whether one cloud quantum computer can be clearly differentiated and identified from another. Analyzes current and historical calibration data from 25 IBM fixed-frequency transmon machines aged a few months to ~2.5 years and finds key features, primarily transmon frequency characteristics, that serve as a unique hardware fingerprint of each machine.
papers.overlap_reason: The only prior work found that addresses the material's provenance problem — 'which physical device actually ran this job?' — as a research question rather than a caveat. Important asymmetry to state explicitly: their method depends on vendor-published per-device calibration data, which is exactly what the material's platform does NOT provide. That makes the material's situation strictly harder and gives it a legitimate gap to claim, but the paper must acknowledge that device fingerprinting from device-intrinsic signatures is an established idea, and should say why it could not be applied (no calibration metadata, and the job may be routed to an arbitrary distributed operator).

papers.title: Decoherence benchmarking of superconducting qubits
papers.authors: Jonathan J. Burnett, Andreas Bengtsson, Marco Scigliuzzo, David Niepce, Marina Kudra, Per Delsing, Jonas Bylander
papers.what_it_establishes: Multi-day statistics on transmon T1, T2* and transition frequency showing all fluctuate, explaining the need for frequent recalibration. Attributes relaxation fluctuations to near-resonant TLS local to each qubit, extracts sub-mHz TLS switching rates, and closes by stating the need for qubit metrology to examine the REPRODUCIBILITY of qubit parameters.
papers.overlap_reason: Foundational multi-day stability result and the origin of the 'we need reproducibility metrology' call the material answers. Establishes that published single-number coherence specs are unrepresentative — background for, but not overlapping with, the material's specific claim that the readout number is both wrong and absent from the spec. Nothing on readout, purity, cloud access or pre-registration.

papers.title: Reproducible coherence characterization of superconducting quantum devices
papers.authors: Corey Rae H. McRae, Gregory M. Stiehl, Haozhi Wang, Sheng-Xiang Lin, Shane A. Caldwell, David P. Pappas, Josh Mutus, Joshua Combes
papers.what_it_establishes: Perspective arguing that comparison of superconducting-device performance metrics ACROSS MEASUREMENTS, DEVICES AND LABORATORIES is currently inaccurate or impossible because of understudied errors from many sources, and outlining what error analysis is required before device optimization can be realized.
papers.overlap_reason: The community-standard framing citation for 'published device metrics are not comparable or reproducible', which is the premise the material builds on. Several co-authors are Rigetti-affiliated, making it apt for a Rigetti-hardware paper. It is a Perspective, not a measurement, so it establishes the problem statement without occupying any of the material's specific results.

papers.title: Purity benchmarking study of error coherence in a superconducting qubit
papers.authors: Auda Zhu, J. H. Béjanin, Xicheng Xu, M. Mariantoni
papers.what_it_establishes: Applies purity benchmarking over 1110 hours on an Xmon qubit at two operating frequencies to separate coherent from incoherent gate error. Finds incoherent errors dominate and are largely frequency-independent (wideband diffusive sources) while coherent errors are strongly sensitive to operating frequency and telegraphic noise, attributed to a single strongly coupled TLS. Reports that purity benchmarking captures dynamics that conventional T1 measurements cannot.
papers.overlap_reason: Flagged because a keyword referee will surface it as 'purity + superconducting + long-term stability'. It is NOT the same quantity: this is purity/unitarity randomized benchmarking, a gate-error-coherence budget, not the state purity Tr[rho^2] of a prepared Bell state measured by a destructive SWAP test. The material should cite it and state the distinction in one clause, both to pre-empt the confusion and because its finding — that a purity-type metric is more sensitive to dynamics than T1 — supports using a purity observable as a drift probe.

papers.title: Error mitigation with stabilized noise in superconducting quantum processors
papers.authors: Young-Seok Kim, Luke C. G. Govia, Andrew Dane, Ewout van den Berg, D. M. Zajac, Bradley Mitchell, Yinyu Liu, Karthik Balakrishnan, George Keefe, Adam Stabile, Emily Pritchett, Jiri Stehlik, et al. (IBM)
papers.what_it_establishes: Shows that learning and maintaining device noise models is complicated by fluctuations over unpredictable timescales arising from resonant qubit-TLS interactions, that these fluctuations degrade noise-model accuracy and hence corrupt observable estimation, and demonstrates experimentally that tuning qubit-TLS interactions reduces noise instability and yields more reliable error mitigation.
papers.overlap_reason: State-of-the-art confirmation that a noise model learned at one time gives incorrect observable estimates at another — the failure mode the material demonstrates with a locked prediction. Strengthens the material's motivation and is a natural 'and industry agrees' citation. No overlap on readout characterization, purity, cloud provenance or pre-registration; and their fix (hardware-level TLS tuning) is unavailable to a Public Tier cloud user, which is worth noting as a scope contrast.

papers.title: Detection of temporal fluctuation in superconducting qubits for quantum error mitigation
papers.authors: Yuta Hirasaki, Shunsuke Daimon, Toshinari Itoko, Naoki Kanazawa, Eiji Saitoh
papers.what_it_establishes: Continuous monitoring of qubit output on an IBM device reveals repeated step-like changes in error rate, each step persisting for several minutes. By correlating the increased errors with anomalous output variance, demonstrates post-selection-based error mitigation, reducing error from 5.4% to 1.6% in a BELL STATE measurement and from 17.5% to 12.0% in a quantum volume circuit.
papers.overlap_reason: Establishes minute-scale, step-like within-session instability on a cloud device and does so on a Bell-state observable, which is the material's within-session drift regime and state. Relevant as the quantitative comparison point for the material's ~1% per-qubit within-session drift. It measures error rate rather than purity, does not pre-register, and does not address cross-session behaviour, readout misspecification or correlated readout. Companion paper (Hirasaki et al., J. Appl. Phys. 136, 2024, 10.1063/5.0226517) attributes the instability to measurement-induced state transitions on tens-of-seconds timescales.

papers.title: Improving Probabilistic Error Cancellation in the Presence of Nonstationary Noise
papers.authors: Samudra Dasgupta, Travis S. Humble
papers.what_it_establishes: Bayesian adaptive strategy to stabilize probabilistic error cancellation under nonstationary noise; experiments with a five-qubit Bernstein-Vazirani implementation on ibm_kolkata show 42% improvement in accuracy and 60% improvement in stability over nonadaptive PEC.
papers.overlap_reason: Extends the two Dasgupta & Humble works the material already cites into hardware-validated adaptive correction under nonstationary noise. Relevant as the 'what one does about it' counterpart to the material's diagnosis, and as evidence that the drift the material reports is treated as actionable rather than merely observed. No overlap on the specific claims.

papers.title: Real-Time Adaptive Tracking of Fluctuating Relaxation Rates in Superconducting Qubits
papers.authors: Fabrizio Berritta, Jacob Benestad, Jan A. Krzywda, Oswin Krause, Malthe A. Marciniak, Svend Krøjer, Christopher Warren, Andreas Nylander, Jonas Bylander, et al.
papers.what_it_establishes: FPGA-based classical controller adaptively and continuously tracks T1 fluctuations of two fixed-frequency transmons, improving temporal resolution by two orders of magnitude over nonadaptive protocols. Reports events in which T1 switches by nearly an order of magnitude over tens of milliseconds rather than minutes or hours as previously reported, with real-time Bayesian estimates in a few milliseconds, and attributes some fast fluctuations to TLS switching at rates up to 10 Hz — four orders of magnitude faster than earlier reports.
papers.overlap_reason: Current state of the art on within-session instability, and a caution for the material: order-of-magnitude T1 switching on tens-of-millisecond timescales means a shot-averaged measurement can silently straddle regimes, which is a mechanism the material's ~1% within-session figure may be averaging over. Worth citing when bounding candidate mechanisms and when justifying that the observed cross-session effect is not fast fluctuation aliased into a session-level statistic. No overlap on readout, purity, cloud provenance or pre-registration.

papers.title: Multiqubit time-varying quantum channels for NISQ-era superconducting quantum processors
papers.authors: Josu Etxezarreta Martínez, Patricio Fuentes, Antonio deMarti iOlius, Javier Garcia-Frias, Javier R. Fonollosa, Pedro M. Crespo
papers.what_it_establishes: Performs a correlation analysis of relaxation-time fluctuations across the qubits of five IBM multiqubit processors and finds it reasonable to assume the fluctuations of T1 and T2 are LOCAL to each qubit rather than correlated across an error-correction block. Defines the fast time-varying quantum channel on that basis and lower-bounds its quantum capacity.
papers.overlap_reason: Supplies the empirical basis for treating drift as per-qubit and independent, which is what the material's '~1% per qubit, propagating to ~0.01 in purity' propagation implicitly assumes. Useful support for that propagation step. It concerns coherence-parameter fluctuation only — no readout, no purity measurement, no cross-session comparison, no provenance.

papers.title: Diagnosing crosstalk in large-scale QPUs using zero-entropy classical shadows
papers.authors: J. A. Montañez-Barrera, Gian Paolo Beretta, Kristel Michielsen, Michael R. von Spakovsky
papers.what_it_establishes: Introduces Zero-Entropy Classical Shadows, using rank-one state reconstruction from classical-shadow data to diagnose noise-induced correlations (crosstalk) across disjoint qubit subsets, applied to ionq_forte (36q), ibm_brisbane (127q) and ibm_fez (156q) with 1000-6000 samples, then used for low-crosstalk qubit selection (10% better solution quality, 33% higher algorithmic coherence on a 20-qubit QAOA).
papers.overlap_reason: Relevant because the material uses a single-copy shadow anchor and reports crosstalk: this establishes that shadow data is already an accepted vehicle for diagnosing device crosstalk at scale on cloud QPUs. It is a crosstalk-diagnosis and qubit-selection tool, not a readout-error characterization or a purity prediction, and it does not pre-register. Cite if the paper frames the shadow anchor as diagnostic rather than merely as a second observable.

papers.title: Error mitigation of BQP computations using measurement-based verification
papers.authors: Joseph Harris, Elham Kashefi
papers.what_it_establishes: A modular error-mitigation protocol for BQP computations under TIME-DEPENDENT noise, built from quantum verification and measurement-based quantum computation, interleaving computation rounds with test rounds for noise sampling and inheriting an exponential bound (in the number of circuit runs) on the probability that the returned classical output is correct. Introduces a post-selection technique called 'basketing' for time-dependent noise; demonstrated in classical noisy simulation with a universal measurement pattern tileable on IBM heavy-hex.
papers.overlap_reason: The closest formal treatment of 'obtaining a trustworthy answer from a device whose behaviour you cannot independently certify and which drifts', which is the material's Bittensor/distributed-operator predicament. Note the important gap: it verifies the COMPUTATION under minimal noise assumptions, not the identity or provenance of the executing hardware, so it does not resolve the material's concern — but a referee is likely to raise it, and the paper is better off distinguishing computation verification from execution-path verification explicitly.

papers.title: Characterizing many-body dynamics with projected ensembles on a superconducting quantum processor
papers.authors: Zhiguang Yan, Zi-Yong Ge, Rui Li, Yu-Ran Zhang, Franco Nori, Yasunobu Nakamura
papers.what_it_establishes: Experimental study of a chaotic many-body system via projected ensembles on a 3D-integrated frequency-tunable superconducting processor; provides direct evidence of deep thermalization by observing a Haar-distributed projected ensemble within a charge-conserved sector, and introduces an ensemble-averaged entropy as a scalable benchmark metric for many-body information leakage to the environment.
papers.overlap_reason: Included because it is the only paper in the citation graph that measures ensemble/moment-type quantities of quantum states on superconducting hardware, and it uses ensemble-averaged entropy as a hardware benchmark — structurally similar to using a purity-type quantity as a device probe. It does not measure state purity via a SWAP test, makes no pre-registered prediction, has full device access, and does not address readout error or drift. Relevance is thematic (moment measurement as hardware benchmark), not claim-level.

papers.title: Dynamics of superconducting qubit relaxation times
papers.authors: Malcolm Carroll, Sami Rosenblatt, Petar Jurcevic, Isaac Lauer, Abhinav Kandala
papers.what_it_establishes: THE SEED. Probes T1 spectrally/temporally via AC-Stark shifts on 10 transmons. Key claim: the ~9-month mean T1 correlates strongly with a single snapshot of the Stark-shifted frequency-averaged T1, i.e. TLS spectral diffusion is 'ergodic-like', so a short snapshot can stand in for a long-time average.
papers.overlap_reason: Same underlying physics (device instability) but it argues the OPPOSITE of the material's headline drift result: an appropriately-averaged snapshot IS representative of months of behaviour. The material must engage with this, because Carroll et al. would predict less session-to-session surprise than ~0.2 in purity on byte-identical circuits. No readout, no purity/moment estimation, no cloud access, no pre-registration.

papers.title: Readout-induced suppression and enhancement of superconducting qubit lifetimes
papers.authors: Ted Thorbeck, Zhihao Xiao, Archana Kamal, Luke C. G. Govia
papers.what_it_establishes: Cites the seed. Explains degradation of qubit lifetime DURING readout as the anti-Zeno effect: readout-induced dephasing broadens the qubit so it overlaps loss 'hot spots' (likely TLS). A self-consistent master equation predicts the lifetime change during readout; both Zeno and anti-Zeno regimes demonstrated.
papers.overlap_reason: Supplies the accepted physical mechanism behind the material's observation that measured readout error is asymmetric in the direction T1 decay during readout predicts, and shows the effect can go either way. It does not report per-qubit assignment-error asymmetry, does not treat neighbour-conditioned crosstalk, and makes no prediction-vs-measurement comparison at the observable level.

papers.title: Purity benchmarking study of error coherence in a single Xmon qubit
papers.authors: Auda Zhu, Jeremy H. Bejanin, Xicheng Xu, Matteo Mariantoni
papers.what_it_establishes: Cites the seed. 1110 hours of purity benchmarking on one Xmon at two operating frequencies. Incoherent errors dominate and are largely frequency-independent; coherent errors are less prevalent but strongly sensitive to operating frequency and telegraph noise, attributed to a single strongly coupled TLS. Purity benchmarking is more sensitive than conventional T1 measurements.
papers.overlap_reason: Name collision rather than substantive overlap: 'purity' here is the RB-family purity-benchmarking decomposition of a single-qubit gate error budget, not the state purity Tr(rho^2) of a prepared Bell state measured by a destructive SWAP test. Worth citing to disambiguate terminology and to avoid a referee assuming the material duplicates it.

papers.title: Adaptive mitigation of time-varying quantum noise
papers.authors: Samudra Dasgupta, Arshag Danageozian, Travis S. Humble
papers.what_it_establishes: Cites the seed. Bayesian inference over a Dirichlet-modelled stochastic Pauli channel to learn and mitigate time-varying noise; reports Bayesian PEC outperforming non-adaptive approaches by ~4.5x in Hellinger distance, and argues that characterizing temporal variation is essential for reliable, reproducible quantum technology.
papers.overlap_reason: Companion to the already-cited Dasgupta and Humble stability papers; useful to complete that citation cluster. No overlap with the readout, purity, specification-omission or pre-registration elements.

papers.title: Quasi-Probabilistic Readout Correction of Mid-Circuit Measurements for Adaptive Feedback via Measurement Randomized Compiling
papers.authors: Akel Hashim, Arnaud Carignan-Dugas, Larry Chen, Christian Juenger, Neelay Fruitwala, Yilun Xu, Gang Huang, Joel J. Wallman, Irfan Siddiqi
papers.what_it_establishes: From an arXiv search-listing snippet only: addresses measurement errors subject to 'non-local correlations due to measurement crosstalk' on superconducting transmons, and presents randomized-compiling-based correction across multiple qubits. I did not read the full abstract page.
papers.overlap_reason: Further evidence that non-local measurement crosstalk is established, characterized and correctable in the superconducting literature — relevant to whether the material's crosstalk observation can be presented as new. Scored from a search snippet only; verify before citing.

papers.title: Statistical methods for single-shot readout discrimination in superconducting qubits
papers.authors: Unknown - not returned by the Semantic Scholar record
papers.venue_year: Unknown (no year or venue in the citation record)
papers.identifier: Semantic Scholar CorpusID:274180826 (no DOI or arXiv id available)
papers.what_it_establishes: Appears in the list of works citing the seed. Title indicates readout-discrimination statistics for superconducting qubits. Repeated attempts to retrieve the abstract were blocked by API rate limiting; I have title and CorpusID only.
papers.overlap_reason: Flagged as a readout-characterization item on the one-hop forward walk that I could not verify. It is the one remaining unchecked candidate on the readout theme and should be resolved manually before the readout-characterization novelty claim is finalized.

papers.title: Mitigation of correlated readout errors without randomized measurements
papers.authors: Adrian Skasberg Aasen, Andras Di Giovanni, Hannes Rotzinger, Alexey V. Ustinov, Martin Gaerttner
papers.what_it_establishes: A readout-error mitigation protocol using only single-qubit Pauli measurements, avoiding randomized measurements, based on complete and efficient characterization of few-qubit correlated POVMs via overlapping detector tomography. Captures a broad class of correlated noise models and is claimed scalable to large registers; validated in simulation up to 100 qubits using readout errors taken from superconducting-qubit experiments.
papers.overlap_reason: Establishes that correlated readout errors are efficiently characterizable and correctable with cheap single-qubit circuits. Relevant because the material's crosstalk-at-each-excitation-weight measurement is effectively a hand-rolled instance of this problem; a referee will ask why an existing overlapping-detector-tomography protocol was not used. Does not touch drift, cross-session variation, pre-registration, or purity observables.

papers.title: Mitigation of readout noise in near-term quantum devices by classical post-processing based on detector tomography
papers.authors: Filip B. Maciejewski, Zoltan Zimboras, Michal Oszmaniec
papers.what_it_establishes: Quantum detector tomography plus classical post-processing to correct readout statistics; run on both IBM AND Rigetti processors; concludes classical noise is the dominant source of readout error.
papers.overlap_reason: Cited by the seed. Uncorrelated/per-detector treatment -- the fetched abstract shows no inter-qubit correlation analysis, so it is superseded on that axis by the same group's 2021 paper. Included mainly because it is one of the few readout-characterization papers that reports on Rigetti hardware, which matters for the material's platform.

papers.title: Probing Context-Dependent Errors in Quantum Processors
papers.authors: Kenneth Rudinger, Timothy Proctor, Dylan Langharst, Mohan Sarovar, Kevin Young, Robin Blume-Kohout
papers.what_it_establishes: Techniques for detecting and quantifying errors whose magnitude depends on context -- what else is happening on the chip, what ran before -- rather than on the target operation alone. Cited by the seed.
papers.overlap_reason: The conceptual precedent for 'the error on qubit A depends on the state of qubit B', which the material's excitation-weight-dependent readout is an instance of. Establishes context dependence as a recognized error class, so the material should present its crosstalk result as a measurement of a known class, not a discovery of one.

papers.title: Accurate and Honest Approximation of Correlated Qubit Noise
papers.authors: F. Setiawan, A. V. Gramolin, Elisha S. Matekole, et al.
papers.what_it_establishes: Title/venue/DOI confirmed via two indexes; I did NOT read the abstract. From title and citation context (cited by the seed alongside its readout-mitigation references), it concerns approximations of correlated qubit noise that remain faithful rather than optimistic.
papers.overlap_reason: Sits in the correlated-noise-modelling neighbourhood the material's crosstalk result occupies. Flagged for the author to read directly -- the 'honest' framing (approximations that do not understate error) could bear on the material's argument that an assumed 2% readout gave a 0.89 prediction where 6.5% gives 0.75. I am not asserting content I did not verify.

papers.title: Loophole-Robust Certification of Quantum Advantage
papers.authors: Prosanta Pal, Gargee Sharma, Ramakrishna Podila
papers.what_it_establishes: Same group as the seed, one month old. Formalizes 'benchmark dependence' to account for classical strategies with correlated side information; bounds classical scores as S_eta <= min{1, S_cl + eta}. On IBM data reports certificates of 0.0812 (CHSH) and 0.2178 (Mermin-GHZ). States that readout-mitigated values are reported separately as sensitivity estimates, and explicitly disclaims modelling time-dependent calibration drift or gate-induced crosstalk; no ZNE, PEC, dynamical decoupling or drift compensation applied.
papers.overlap_reason: The seed's own follow-on and the only plausible citing candidate. From the arXiv abstract page it does not appear to cite arXiv:2601.08290, but the HTML bibliography was truncated on fetch so I cannot confirm this either way -- treat as unresolved. Relevant chiefly as evidence of where this group is heading, and because its explicit disclaimer about not modelling drift or crosstalk is a live opening the material's results speak to.

papers.title: Characterizing correlated noise with single-qubit operations
papers.authors: Balazs Gulacsi, Joris Kattemoelle, et al.
papers.what_it_establishes: Title, venue, date confirmed via OpenAlex citing-set of Setiawan 2025; abstract NOT read.
papers.overlap_reason: Recent entry in the correlated-noise characterization line, surfaced by the co-citation hop. Listed for completeness of the prior-art boundary on correlated noise measurement; I make no claim about its contents.

papers.title: Detecting and tracking drift in quantum information processors
papers.authors: Timothy Proctor, Melissa Revelle, Erik Nielsen, Kenneth Rudinger, Daniel Lobser, Peter Maunz, Robin Blume-Kohout, Kevin Young
papers.what_it_establishes: A fast, statistically sound spectral-analysis technique for resolving time dependence in quantum processors, applicable to time-series data from any quantum processor experiment and to randomized benchmarking, gate set tomography and Ramsey spectroscopy. Demonstrated on simulations and trapped-ion experiments. Cited BY the seed.
papers.overlap_reason: Supplies the standard statistical machinery for establishing that drift is present and for separating timescales — the tool a referee will expect the material to have considered when claiming a ~20x cross-session/within-session ratio. The abstract does not address session-boundary structure or superconducting cloud access, and the demonstration is trapped-ion. Relevant as method prior art, not as a competing result.

papers.title: Mitigation of correlated readout errors without randomized measurements
papers.authors: Adrian Skasberg Aasen, Andras Di Giovanni, Hannes Rotzinger, Alexey V. Ustinov, Martin Gärttner
papers.what_it_establishes: A readout error-mitigation protocol using only single-qubit Pauli measurements, covering a broad class of correlated noise models and scalable to large systems; validated in simulations up to 100 qubits using readout errors obtained from experiments with superconducting qubits.
papers.overlap_reason: Current state of the art for handling correlated readout error, so it bounds any claim the material might make about needing new mitigation machinery. It is a mitigation method validated largely in simulation from experimentally derived error data; the webpage content gave no evidence it measures excitation-weight dependence or saturation on hardware, which is the material's specific characterization claim.

papers.title: Rigorous measurement error correction
papers.authors: Michael R. Geller
papers.what_it_establishes: Shows that nonideal measurement of an arbitrary n-qubit state is equivalent to ideal projective measurement followed by a classical Markov process Gamma, with Gamma obtainable from gate set tomography. Cited BY the seed.
papers.overlap_reason: The formal justification for the material's readout-feedback correction step (treating measured readout as a classical stochastic map applied after ideal measurement). I could NOT verify from the abstract whether the formalism as presented captures inter-qubit correlations or what the calibration-circuit scaling is; the fetched page did not answer either question. Flagging that limitation rather than asserting coverage.

papers.title: Computational Performance Bounds Prediction in Quantum Computing With Unstable Noise (QuBound)
papers.authors: Jinyang Li, Samudra Dasgupta, Yuhong Song, Lei Yang, Travis S. Humble, Weiwen Jiang
papers.venue_year: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems (2025); arXiv 22 Jul 2025
papers.what_it_establishes: Predicts computational performance BOUNDS (rather than point predictions) for circuits under on-the-fly, time-varying noise, using an encoder plus LSTM over circuit and noise information; reports ranges over 10x narrower than analytical alternatives.
papers.overlap_reason: The state of the art for what a prediction under nonstationary noise should look like, and an implicit argument that point predictions of the kind the material pre-registered are the wrong object. Useful for the material's discussion of why its prediction missed. No hardware validation devices are named in the abstract; no pre-registration; no readout characterization.

papers.title: Fast-tracking and disentangling of qubit noise fluctuations using minimal-data averaging and hierarchical discrete fluctuation auto-segmentation
papers.authors: Abhishek Agarwal, Lachlan P. Lindoy, Deep Lall, Sebastian E. de Graaf, Tobias Lindström, Ivan Rungger
papers.what_it_establishes: Tracks and disentangles transmon qubit frequency fluctuations at a temporal resolution of tens of milliseconds over hours, separating overlapping noise sources including charge-parity and two-level-system switching.
papers.overlap_reason: Covers the WITHIN-session timescale the material measures at ~1% per qubit, and gives a microscopic account (TLS, charge parity) of what drives it. The abstract does not distinguish within-session from cross-session drift, which is precisely the contrast the material rests on, so it does not pre-empt the ~20x claim — but it is the paper a referee will point to when asking whether the material's mechanism bounding excluded TLS switching.

papers.title: Stability of Quantum Computers (PhD dissertation)
papers.authors: Samudra Dasgupta
papers.what_it_establishes: Consolidated treatment of the seed's research programme on transmon processors, framed around non-stationary noise parameter distributions across time and qubits.
papers.overlap_reason: The single most complete statement of the prior stability literature the material is positioned against; useful as a one-citation anchor for 'this problem is established'. I could not verify from the abstract whether it treats readout error specifically or cross-session reproducibility, so I am not claiming it does.

papers.title: Simon's algorithm in the NISQ cloud
papers.authors: Reece Robertson, Emery Doucet, Ernest Spicer, Sebastian Deffner
papers.what_it_establishes: Uses Simon's algorithm to benchmark error rates of devices currently available in the quantum cloud (IBM and IonQ), emphasizing that device architecture and chip topology matter when transpiling, and concluding that two-qubit operations on spatially separated qubits on superconducting chips should be avoided.
papers.overlap_reason: A user-side cloud benchmarking study of the same genre as the material, and its 'avoid spatially separated qubits' finding is relevant background for a twelve-chiplet device where register placement across chiplet boundaries is a candidate mechanism for the n=3/n=4 ordering flip. Different algorithm, no purity, no pre-registration, no session analysis.

papers.title: Scaling Superconducting Quantum Computers with Chiplet Architectures
papers.authors: Kaitlin N. Smith, Gokul Subramanian Ravi, Jonathan M. Baker, Frederic T. Chong
papers.venue_year: MICRO 2022 (IEEE/ACM International Symposium on Microarchitecture); arXiv Oct 2022
papers.what_it_establishes: Analysis of tiling multiple small superconducting chips into a larger processor, and the architectural consequences of inter-chiplet links.
papers.overlap_reason: The Cepheus-1-108Q is twelve nine-qubit chiplets, so chiplet-boundary structure is a live candidate mechanism for the material's non-monotonicity (an n=4 register spanning a chiplet edge while the nested n=3 register does not, or vice versa). This is background the material's mechanism-bounding section should engage, not competing prior art. Verified only at abstract level via citation metadata.

papers.title: A Review and Collection of Metrics and Benchmarks for Quantum Computers: definitions, methodologies and software
papers.authors: Not verified beyond the record (multi-author review)
papers.what_it_establishes: A comprehensive collection of benchmarks for holistic comparison of quantum computers, from individual hardware components to whole applications, with a consistent definition format; identifies five areas for international standardization working groups, explicitly including inter-laboratory measurement methodology studies and REPRODUCIBILITY STANDARDS.
papers.overlap_reason: Useful as the community-standards hook for the material's argument that specifications should publish readout error. I could NOT verify from the abstract whether it covers drift metrics, readout characterization, or vendor-spec-versus-user-measurement, and the fetch explicitly declined to confirm those — do not cite it for any specific claim without reading the full text. Author list not verified; do not cite until checked.

papers.title: Toward Consistent High-Fidelity Quantum Learning on Unstable Devices via Efficient In-Situ Calibration (QuPAD)
papers.authors: Zhirui Hu, Robert Wolle, Mingzhen Tian, Qiang Guan, Travis S. Humble, Weiwen Jiang
papers.what_it_establishes: Addresses that noise on quantum devices is not stable by calibrating pulse amplitude and duration of each Rzx gate at runtime, reporting large accuracy gains (59.33% on classification, 66.34% closer to ground state energy) with 8-10 qubit device runtimes under 15 minutes.
papers.overlap_reason: Represents the standard prescriptive response to instability — recalibrate in situ — which is the obvious referee question against a pre-registered study that cannot re-run. Cite when explaining why the pre-registration design deliberately forgoes adaptive recalibration. No device names in the abstract; no session-boundary analysis; no readout characterization.

papers.title: Characterizing the Stability of NISQ Devices
papers.authors: Samudra Dasgupta, Travis S. Humble
papers.venue_year: IEEE International Conference on Quantum Computing and Engineering (QCE), 2020
papers.what_it_establishes: The first paper of the seed's programme, characterizing NISQ device stability. Cited BY the seed.

papers.title: Accrediting outputs of noisy intermediate-scale quantum computing devices
papers.authors: Samuele Ferracin, Theodoros Kapourniotis, Animesh Datta
papers.venue_year: New Journal of Physics 21, 113038 (2019); arXiv Nov 2018
papers.what_it_establishes: A protocol to accredit the outputs of a NISQ device — bounding the variation distance of returned outputs from the correct distribution — without requiring trust in the device's internal operation. Cited BY the seed.
papers.overlap_reason: The most relevant existing answer to the material's untrusted-execution-path problem: accreditation gives output guarantees without needing to verify which machine ran the job or how. A referee asking 'how can you claim anything when you cannot verify the execution path' will expect this literature to be acknowledged. Author list taken from the citation record, not independently verified; content not read beyond the citation entry.

papers.title: Detecting and tracking drift in quantum information processors
papers.authors: Timothy Proctor, Melissa Revelle, Erik Nielsen, Kenneth Rudinger, Daniel Lobser, Peter Maunz, Robin Blume-Kohout, Kevin Young
papers.what_it_establishes: SEED. Spectral (Fourier) analysis of time-series characterization data to detect, localize and track time-dependent errors, applied to randomized benchmarking, gate set tomography and Ramsey spectroscopy, on simulation and trapped-ion data. Establishes that the standard characterization toolkit assumes static error rates and that this assumption is routinely violated.
papers.overlap_reason: Owns the general claim that QIP errors drift and that drift must be detected before characterization is trusted. Does not touch readout characterization, cloud access, provenance, purity/moment measurement, or pre-registration. The material's within-session ~1% drift is the regime this paper's method addresses; its cross-session ~0.2 purity effect is not.

papers.title: Fluctuations of Energy-Relaxation Times in Superconducting Qubits
papers.authors: P. V. Klimov, J. Kelly, Z. Chen, et al.
papers.what_it_establishes: CITED BY SEED. T1 in superconducting qubits fluctuates on hour timescales due to interaction with two-level-system defects.
papers.overlap_reason: Supplies a published physical mechanism for the material's session-scale degradation and for T1-driven readout asymmetry. Useful as the mechanism citation; establishes nothing about readout crosstalk, purity, or cloud reproducibility. Title and venue verified via Crossref (INSPIRE returned this reference without a title).

papers.title: Quantum tomography for non-iid sources
papers.authors: Leonardo Zambrano
papers.what_it_establishes: CITES SEED. Projected least-squares tomography remains statistically optimal under fully adaptive (non-i.i.d.) state and channel preparation; sample complexity for the time-averaged object matches optimal i.i.d. scaling. Dropping i.i.d. changes the interpretation of the reconstructed object, not the fundamental sample complexity.
papers.overlap_reason: Companion to the above for tomography rather than shadows. Relevant chiefly for its interpretive point — under drift you are estimating a time-averaged object — which bears on what the material's cross-session purity numbers actually mean.

papers.title: Benchmarking quantum computers
papers.authors: Timothy Proctor, Kevin Young, Andrew D. Baczewski, Robin Blume-Kohout
papers.what_it_establishes: CITES SEED. Review of the quantum computer benchmarking field by the seed paper's own group. Abstract not available in OpenAlex; I did not retrieve the arXiv abstract, so my characterization rests on title, venue and authorship only.
papers.overlap_reason: The standard framing citation for what benchmarking claims are and are not licensed to say. Relevant to how the material positions a single-device, single-platform study, but establishes no specific result the material duplicates. Flagged as weakly verified: I confirmed existence, venue and authorship but not content.

papers.title: A Practical Introduction to Benchmarking and Characterization of Quantum Computers
papers.authors: Akel Hashim, Long B. Nguyen, Noah Goss, Brian Marinelli, Ravi K. Naik, Trevor Chistolini, Jordan Hines, J. P. Marceaux, et al.
papers.what_it_establishes: CITES SEED. Tutorial and reference covering QCVV principles and protocols from basic qubit characterization to advanced benchmarking, with discussion of each protocol's advantages, disadvantages and scalability.
papers.overlap_reason: Reference work establishing what the standard characterization toolkit contains. Useful for justifying that the material's diagnostic steps are standard practice; contributes no competing result.

papers.title: Investigation of Hardware Architecture Effects on Quantum Algorithm Performance: A Comparative Hardware Study
papers.authors: Askar Oralkhan, Temirlan Zhaxalykov
papers.what_it_establishes: Benchmarks five algorithms (Bell, GHZ, QFT, Grover, QAOA) across trapped-ion, superconducting and simulator backends via Amazon Braket, reporting fidelity, CHSH violation and success probability. Reports 10-qubit GHZ fidelity above 0.8 on trapped-ion versus below 0.15 on superconducting platforms. Opens by noting that identical quantum circuits may behave substantially differently across cloud devices.
papers.overlap_reason: Same genre (cloud-accessible device comparison, identical circuits behaving differently) but the axis of comparison is across platforms rather than across sessions on one device, and there is no pre-registration, readout characterization, or drift analysis. Included because it is the nearest published instance of the 'identical circuits, different answers on cloud hardware' framing.

papers.title: Qubit readout error mitigation with bit-flip averaging
papers.authors: Alistair W. R. Smith, Kiran E. Khosla, Chris N. Self, M. S. Kim
papers.what_it_establishes: Readout error mitigation that symmetrizes the readout error channel by bit-flip averaging, reducing the calibration data required and removing the need to characterize the full asymmetric response matrix.
papers.overlap_reason: Cited by the seed. Prior art on handling asymmetric and correlated readout error, but it MITIGATES the error rather than measuring it as a device-characterization gap. The material's asymmetry-in-the-T1-direction observation is consistent with, not anticipated by, this work.

papers.title: Experimental accreditation of outputs of noisy quantum computers
papers.authors: Samuele Ferracin, Seth T. Merkel, David C. McKay, Animesh Datta
papers.what_it_establishes: An accreditation protocol upper-bounding the variation distance between noisy and noiseless output distributions of arbitrary quantum computations, demonstrated on 24 circuits on superconducting hardware.
papers.overlap_reason: Cited by the seed. Provides a rigorous alternative route to trusting a hardware output without a device specification, which is a competing methodology for the material's problem. Bounds distributions rather than predicting a specific observable, and does not diagnose which physical input is wrong.

papers.title: Theory of Quantum System Certification

papers.what_it_establishes: Tutorial/review of protocols for certifying the physical layer of quantum devices described by quantum states and processes, with emphasis on near-term devices.
papers.overlap_reason: Cited by the seed. Standard reference for the certification framing; supplies vocabulary but no overlapping empirical result.

papers.title: Reliability and reproducibility in computational science: implementing validation, verification and uncertainty quantification in silico
papers.authors: Peter V. Coveney, Derek Groen, Alfons G. Hoekstra
