papers.what_it_establishes: Cross-disciplinary framing of validation, verification and uncertainty quantification as the basis for reliable and reproducible computational science.
papers.overlap_reason: Cited by the seed. This is the nearest thing in the seed's own reference list to the material's pre-registration argument, but it argues for V&V/UQ practice generally and does not propose or perform pre-registration of predictions.

papers.title: Dependable classical-quantum computing systems engineering
papers.authors: Edoardo Giusto, Santiago Nunez-Corrales, Kaitlin N. Smith, Travis S. Humble, Samudra Dasgupta et al.
papers.what_it_establishes: A dependability framework for hybrid classical-quantum systems, importing reliability/availability/maintainability engineering concepts into quantum computing system design.
papers.overlap_reason: Cites the seed. Provides the systems-engineering vocabulary (dependability, trustworthiness) the material could adopt for its unverifiable-execution-path discussion, but contains no competing measurement.

papers.title: Simon's Algorithm in the NISQ Cloud
papers.authors: Reece Robertson, Emery Doucet, Ernest Spicer, Sebastian Deffner
papers.what_it_establishes: Uses Simon's algorithm to benchmark error rates of cloud-available IBM and IonQ devices, giving an objective cross-platform comparison and showing transpilation/topology strongly govern observed performance.
papers.overlap_reason: Cites the seed. Same genre (a user-side cloud hardware study reporting what you actually get), but the target is algorithmic success rate across vendors, not a pre-registered observable, and readout is not the diagnosed failing input.

papers.title: Toward Consistent High-Fidelity Quantum Learning on Unstable Devices via Efficient In-Situ Calibration
papers.authors: Zhirui Hu, Robert Wolle, Mingzhen Tian, Qiang Guan, Travis S. Humble, Weiwen Jiang
papers.what_it_establishes: Shows device noise changes dynamically over time and proposes efficient run-time in-situ calibration to maintain consistent fidelity for variational/quantum-learning workloads.
papers.overlap_reason: Cites the seed. Confirms that stale calibration is a recognized, actively engineered-around problem, which supports but does not pre-empt the material's diagnosis.

papers.title: Scalable Mitigation of Measurement Errors on Quantum Computers
papers.authors: Paul D. Nation, Hwajung Kang, Neereja Sundaresan, Jay M. Gambetta
papers.what_it_establishes: Matrix-free (M3) measurement error mitigation working in the subspace of observed bitstrings, handling both uncorrelated and correlated errors with accurate error bounds and O(1) iterative convergence.
papers.overlap_reason: Standard readout-mitigation prior art. Relevant because the material's correction is applied to the PREDICTION rather than to the data; the contrast with standard mitigation should be stated explicitly.

papers.title: Detecting crosstalk errors in quantum information processors
papers.authors: Mohan Sarovar, Timothy Proctor, Kenneth Rudinger, Kevin Young, Erik Nielsen, Robin Blume-Kohout
papers.what_it_establishes: A comprehensive framework for defining, modelling and detecting crosstalk errors, which produce correlated and nonlocal errors that are especially harmful because they violate locality assumptions.
papers.overlap_reason: The definitional reference for crosstalk as a correlated error class. The material's excitation-conditioned readout observation is an instance of this class; the framework does not supply the specific measurement.

papers.title: Practical Introduction to Benchmarking and Characterization of Quantum Computers
papers.authors: Akel Hashim, Long B. Nguyen, Noah Goss, Brian Marinelli, Ravi Naik, Trevor Chistolini, Jordan Hines, J. P. Marceaux et al.
papers.what_it_establishes: Tutorial review of quantum characterization, verification and validation (QCVV): core models, measurement and process concepts, and the standard toolset for scrutinizing device performance.
papers.overlap_reason: The current standard reference for what a properly characterized device report should contain. Useful as the benchmark against which the material can argue that the Cepheus specification is incomplete.

papers.title: Readout error mitigated quantum state tomography tested on superconducting qubits
papers.authors: Adrian Aasen, Andrea Di Giovanni, Hannes Rotzinger, Alexey V. Ustinov, Martin Gaerttner
papers.what_it_establishes: Tests readout error mitigation for quantum state tomography on superconducting qubits, arguing that current experiments are limited by noise sources only partially captured by simple analytical models and that additional characterization of noise sources is required.
papers.overlap_reason: Independently supports the material's central assertion that simple analytical noise models built from published parameters are insufficient and that additional readout characterization is needed. It mitigates rather than predicts, and does not measure purity.

papers.title: Anchor: Reducing Temporal and Spatial Output Performance Variability on Quantum Computers
papers.authors: Yuqian Huo, Daniel Leeds, Jason Ludmir, Nicholas S. DiBrita, Tirthak Patel
papers.venue_year: Proc. ACM Meas. Anal. Comput. Syst. (POMACS) / ACM SIGMETRICS 2026; arXiv Oct 2025
papers.what_it_establishes: Proposes 'Anchor', a linear-programming shot-allocation technique that spreads a circuit's shots across multiple qubit maps to REDUCE variance in output fidelity (TVD), claiming 73% variability reduction over noise-adaptive mapping. Its variability EVIDENCE is thin and IBM-only: Fig.3 shows TVD of a 4-qubit VAR circuit over five days on ibm_hanoi (temporal) and across five 27-qubit IBM machines on one day (spatial); the bulk of the evaluation is Qiskit AerSimulator (20 algorithms x 4 techniques x 100 runs = 8000 sim runs) with real-hardware validation on five IBM machines over two-day periods, plus a TVD predictor trained on 289,107 random circuits.
papers.overlap_reason: Same phenomenon class (temporal + spatial output variability on cloud NISQ) and a useful vocabulary source, but it is a MITIGATION technique, not a characterization study, and it shares almost nothing else with the material. I parsed the full body text: it contains ZERO occurrences of 'readout', 'Rigetti', 'purity', 'pre-regist', 'session'. It never attributes variability to a mechanism, never compares measured to published device specs, never runs the same circuit across sessions, and its temporal scale is days on one IBM machine, not the material's cross-session 0.2-in-purity swings on byte-identical circuits. It does not touch pre-registration, purity/moment measurement, or provider verifiability.

papers.title: Mitigation of correlated readout errors without randomized measurements
papers.authors: Adrian Skasberg Aasen, Andras Di Giovanni, Hannes Rotzinger, A. V. Ustinov, Martin Gaerttner
papers.what_it_establishes: A readout-error mitigation protocol using only single-qubit Pauli measurements, avoiding randomized measurements, based on complete and efficient characterization of few-qubit correlated POVMs via overlapping detector tomography; captures a broad class of correlated noise models; assessed in simulation up to 100 qubits using readout errors taken from superconducting-qubit experiments.
papers.overlap_reason: Current state of the art on correlated-readout characterization and mitigation, so it fixes where the field stands in 2025-26 and makes clear that 'readout errors are correlated' is settled. But the paper's contribution is a mitigation protocol validated largely in simulation; it does not report a device specification omitting readout, a pre-registered prediction, or session-scale drift. Cite for completeness of the readout-correlation literature.

papers.title: Detecting crosstalk errors in quantum information processors
papers.authors: Mohan Sarovar, Timothy Proctor, Kenneth Rudinger, Kevin Young, Erik Nielsen, Robin Blume-Kohout
papers.what_it_establishes: Gives a rigorous definition of crosstalk error capturing the disparate physical phenomena called 'crosstalk', a concrete model of crosstalk-free processes, and a protocol for detecting and LOCALIZING crosstalk errors; notes such errors are correlated and nonlocal and especially harmful where error correction assumes locality.
papers.overlap_reason: Definitional prior art. If the material calls its excitation-dependent readout dependence 'crosstalk', this is the reference that fixes what that word means and how one demonstrates it rather than asserting it. No overlap on results -- it is a framework paper and does not treat readout specifically or measure any device the material used.

papers.title: Scaling Qubit Readout with Hardware Efficient Machine Learning Architectures
papers.authors: Satvik Maurya, Chaithanya Naik Mude, William D. Oliver, Benjamin Lienhard, Swamit S. Tannu
papers.venue_year: ISCA 2023 (50th Annual Int. Symp. on Computer Architecture); arXiv:2212.03895
papers.what_it_establishes: States that on state-of-the-art superconducting processors readout errors range from 1-10%, and enumerates their causes as CROSSTALK, spontaneous state transitions, and EXCITATION CAUSED BY THE READOUT PULSE. Proposes hardware-efficient ML discriminator architectures for higher readout accuracy.
papers.overlap_reason: Two useful anchors for the material. First, the published 1-10% range makes the material's measured ~6.5% per qubit unremarkable AS A VALUE -- which sharpens rather than weakens the point, because the complaint is that the specification omits the number, not that the number is exotic. Second, the enumerated mechanisms (crosstalk, readout-pulse-induced excitation) independently support the material's attribution to T1 decay during readout and neighbour excitation. No overlap on method: this is a discriminator-design paper, not a device characterization.

papers.title: Quantum Computing in the Cloud: Analyzing job and machine characteristics
papers.authors: Gokul Subramanian Ravi, Kaitlin N. Smith, Pranav Gokhale, Frederic T. Chong
papers.venue_year: IEEE Int. Symp. on Workload Characterization (IISWC) 2021; arXiv:2203.13121
papers.what_it_establishes: First academic study of resource consumption and execution characteristics on quantum cloud systems: IBM Quantum over a two-year period, >6000 jobs, >600,000 circuit executions, ~10 billion shots, 20+ machines; analyzes execution times, queueing/wait behaviour and utilization.
papers.overlap_reason: Establishes what is normally observable about a cloud quantum job and the scale at which the community expects such studies to be done. Relevant chiefly as contrast: the material's platform provides LESS provenance than the IBM cloud Ravi et al. mined (no per-job calibration metadata, no verifiable execution path), which is a defensible framing for why the material is a characterization-of-the-access-path study. No overlap on readout, purity, or stability results.

papers.title: Experimental Evaluation of Xanadu X8 Photonic Quantum Computer: Error Measurement, Characterization, and Implications
papers.authors: Aditya Ranjan, Tirthak Patel, Harshitta Gandhi, Daniel Silver, William Cutler, Devesh Tiwari
papers.what_it_establishes: First independent characterization of Xanadu's X8 photonic quantum computer, presented as an important step toward practical and scalable photonic machines.
papers.overlap_reason: Genre precedent, not content overlap: it shows this venue lineage accepts 'first independent characterization of a specific commercial platform' as a contribution in its own right, which is the strongest framing available for the material. Different platform, different error physics, no readout-correlation or pre-registration content.

papers.title: Benchmarking the quality of multiplexed qubit readout beyond assignment fidelity
papers.authors: Andras Di Giovanni, Adrian Skasberg Aasen, Juergen Lisenfeld, et al.
papers.what_it_establishes: Argues assignment fidelity is an insufficient summary of readout quality for MULTIPLEXED readout and proposes richer benchmarks. (Content beyond title/venue not read in full.)
papers.overlap_reason: Directly on the material's implicit thesis that a single published readout number -- or in the material's case, no number at all -- fails to describe multi-qubit readout. Multiplexed readout is the physical origin of the neighbour dependence the material measures. I did not read the abstract in full, so treat this as a lead to verify rather than a settled claim.

papers.title: Repetition-code-based readout error detection and correction across hardware platforms and generations
papers.authors: Csaba Czaban, Orsolya Kalman, Sergey N. Filippov, Zoltan Zimboras
papers.what_it_establishes: Encodes data qubits with ancillas before measurement and decodes by post-selection or majority voting, correcting readout errors at the level of INDIVIDUAL SHOTS rather than in aggregate post-processing. Improves readout fidelity across IBM Heron r1-r3 and Quantinuum H1/H2; superconducting devices show diminishing returns from added redundancy because of gate errors, trapped ions benefit from larger code distances.
papers.overlap_reason: Current-generation readout work spanning multiple platforms and hardware GENERATIONS, so it is the natural place a referee will look for 'how bad is readout in 2026'. Relevant to the material's mitigation discussion, not to its findings: no vendor-specification comparison, no session drift, no purity target.

papers.title: Trust, but Verify: Preregistered Assurance for Quantum Results -- A Helium VQE Testbed Across Two IBM Heron Processors
papers.authors: Amit Brahmbhatt (Quantum Clarity LLC)
papers.venue_year: Zenodo record, 28 June 2026 -- SELF-PUBLISHED, NOT PEER REVIEWED, zero citations
papers.what_it_establishes: Declares an 'invariant contract' -- physical invariants, tolerances and a decision rule serialized to canonical JSON and bound by a SHA-256 digest -- BEFORE observing outcomes, yielding ACCEPT / FLAG / CAN'T-CERTIFY verdicts. Run on ibm_kingston and ibm_fez (156-qubit Heron r2), ~28 quantum-seconds, contract 'helium_vqe_v1' with a published digest encoding an energy lower bound (1.6 mHa), particle number (+/-0.05 e) and spin projection (+/-0.05 hbar).
papers.overlap_reason: The ONLY item I found anywhere that pre-commits a quantum hardware prediction cryptographically before execution, so it is the material's nearest neighbour on the pre-registration axis and a referee could surface it. TREAT WITH CARE: it is a self-published Zenodo record from a single-author LLC with no peer review and no citations, and the same author has several similar Zenodo items; I verified only the record page, not any result. Different target entirely (VQE energy invariants, IBM Heron) and it certifies rather than predicts a physical quantity, so it does not anticipate the material's locked purity prediction or its diagnosis.

papers.title: TLS Dynamics in a Superconducting Qubit Due to Background Ionizing Radiation
papers.authors: Ted Thorbeck, Andrew Eddins, Isaac Lauer, Douglas T. McClure, Malcolm Carroll
papers.what_it_establishes: Investigates how ionizing radiation and two-level-system dynamics interact to produce fluctuations in superconducting qubit lifetimes and device reliability.
papers.overlap_reason: A candidate physical MECHANISM for the material's cross-session drift and, more pointedly, for its non-monotonicity -- TLS defects are qubit-local and reshuffle on hour-to-day timescales, which is one of the few mechanisms that can make an n=3 register heal (0.317 -> 0.378 -> 0.587) while a superset n=4 register degrades (0.431 -> 0.420 -> 0.382) and their ordering flips. If TLS is among the seven mechanisms the material bounded or excluded, this is the reference; if not, it is a gap. No overlap on results.

papers.title: Software Mitigation of Crosstalk on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum Computers
papers.authors: Prakash Murali, David C. McKay, Margaret Martonosi, Ali Javadi-Abhari

papers.authors: Swamit S. Tannu, Moinuddin K. Qureshi

papers.title: Dependable classical-quantum computing systems engineering
papers.authors: Edoardo Giusto, Santiago Núñez-Corrales, Kaitlin N. Smith, Phuong Cao, Ed Younis, Paolo Rech, Flavio Vella, Betis Baheri, Alessandro Cilardo, Bartolomeo Montrucchio, Weiwen Jiang, Shuai Xu, Samudra Dasgupta, Ravishankar K. Iyer, Travis S. Humble et al.

papers.title: When quantum tomography goes wrong: drift of quantum sources and other errors
papers.authors: S. J. van Enk, Robin Blume-Kohout
papers.identifier: New J. Phys. 15, 025024 (2013); cited as ref [42] of arXiv:2307.06833
papers.what_it_establishes: Shows that drift in a quantum source corrupts tomographic reconstruction and that standard tomography can silently return wrong answers when the source is non-stationary.

Predates cloud hardware and says nothing about readout disclosure or pre-registration. VERIFICATION CAVEAT: verified from the seed's reference list only; abstract not read.

papers.title: Impact of time-correlated noise on zero-noise extrapolation
papers.authors: Kevin Schultz, Ryan LaRose, Andrea Mari, Gregory Quiroz, Nathan Shammah, B. David Clader, William J. Zeng
papers.identifier: Phys. Rev. A 106, 052406 (2022); cited as ref [36] of arXiv:2307.06833

Supports the material's drift framing but overlaps none of its measurements. VERIFICATION CAVEAT: verified from the seed's reference list only.

papers.authors: Xiao Shi, Jiyu Jiang, Xian Wu, Jingu Xie, Hongshun Yao, Xin Wang

Method/efficiency paper; no prediction accountability, no drift, no readout disclosure. VERIFICATION CAVEAT: search-listing snippet only.

papers.title: Probing quantum telecloning on superconducting quantum processors
papers.authors: Elijah Pelofske, Andreas Bärtschi, Stephan Eidenbenz, Bryan Garcia, Boris Kiefer

VERIFICATION CAVEAT: verified from the seed's reference list only.

papers.title: Anchor: Reducing Temporal and Spatial Output Performance Variability on Quantum Computers
papers.authors: Yuqian Huo, Daniel Leeds, Jason Ludmir, Nicholas S. DiBrita, Tirthak Patel
papers.venue_year: ACM SIGMETRICS 2026 / Proc. ACM Meas. Anal. Comput. Syst.; arXiv Oct 2025

papers.title: Interacting defects generate stochastic fluctuations in superconducting qubits
papers.authors: Jeremy H. Bejanin, Catherine T. Earnest, Ahmad S. Sharafeldin, Matteo Mariantoni
papers.what_it_establishes: CITED BY THE SEED. Measures energy relaxation of a frequency-tunable planar transmon over time AND frequency across a few days, reproducing the observed stochastic patterns with a model of the qubit coupled to high-frequency TLS which in turn interact with thermally activated low-frequency TLS. Infers the low-frequency TLS density is ~3 orders of magnitude larger.
papers.overlap_reason: Supplies a concrete microscopic model capable of producing multi-day, non-stationary, non-monotonic device behaviour — directly useful for the material's mechanism-bounding exercise, and a candidate explanation for the n=3 healing / n=4 degrading divergence that neither readout nor gate count can produce. Mechanism-side only; no circuit-level, readout, or reproducibility claim.

papers.title: Correlated charge noise and relaxation errors in superconducting qubits
papers.authors: C. D. Wilen, S. Abdullah, N. A. Kurinsky, et al., R. McDermott
papers.what_it_establishes: CITED BY THE SEED. Characterizes a superconducting multiqubit circuit and finds charge noise HIGHLY CORRELATED over a length scale exceeding 600 micrometres, with discrete charge jumps accompanied by strong transient reduction of qubit energy relaxation time.
papers.overlap_reason: Establishes that device errors can be spatially correlated over macroscopic distances via a shared substrate mechanism — a candidate explanation for register-level effects that per-qubit models cannot produce, which is precisely the class the material's n=3/n=4 non-monotonicity falls into. Physical-mechanism prior art for the material's exclusion analysis; no overlap with readout characterization, purity estimation, or the cloud/provenance argument.

papers.title: Resolving catastrophic error bursts from cosmic rays in large arrays of superconducting qubits
papers.authors: Matt McEwen, Lara Faoro, Kunal Arya, et al. (Google Quantum AI)
papers.what_it_establishes: CITED BY THE SEED. Uses space- and time-resolved measurement on a large qubit array to show that impinging high-energy particles ionize the substrate and induce quasiparticle bursts that destroy coherence device-wide, violating the independence assumption underpinning error correction.
papers.overlap_reason: A second device-wide correlated-error mechanism to bound or exclude. Relevant to the material only as a candidate for abrupt session-to-session changes; timescales (millisecond-to-second bursts) are a poor match for the material's ~0.2 purity shift persisting across whole sessions, which likely lets the material EXCLUDE it cleanly. No claim overlap.

papers.title: Time-varying quantum channel models for superconducting qubits
papers.authors: Josu Etxezarreta Martinez, Patricio Fuentes, Pedro Crespo, Javier Garcia-Frias
papers.what_it_establishes: CITED BY THE SEED; its direct predecessor. Establishes that conventional STATIC quantum channel models with fixed T1/T2 do not capture realistic superconducting-qubit noise with sufficient precision, and introduces time-varying quantum channel (TVQC) models as a more faithful portrayal of decoherence.
papers.overlap_reason: The foundational statement that a single fixed noise specification misrepresents a real superconducting device — the general principle behind the material's finding that a published median-fidelity spec sheet fails to predict a measured outcome. But the failure mode it formalizes is coherence-parameter time-variation, whereas the material's dominant failure was a MISSING parameter (readout, unpublished and ~3x the assumed value) rather than a drifting one. Related framing, different diagnosis.

papers.title: Verified delegated quantum computation requires techniques beyond cut-and-choose
papers.authors: Not verified — I did not retrieve the author list
papers.what_it_establishes: Concerns delegated quantum computation, in which a client with limited quantum capability outsources computation to an untrusted quantum server while preserving correctness and privacy, and argues that verification requires techniques beyond cut-and-choose. Represents the cryptographic verification tradition (blind and verifiable delegated quantum computing).
papers.overlap_reason: Included to close the lens rather than because it competes. The cryptographic verification literature (this, plus verifiable blind quantum computing generally) proves what a client CAN certify about an untrusted server in principle, under protocol assumptions the material's setup does not satisfy — the material submitted plain OpenQASM through a commercial aggregator with no verification protocol. Different problem, different assumptions, no result in contention. Worth one sentence in Related Work only to say why this tradition does not apply.

papers.title: Optimal Quantum Purity Amplification
papers.authors: Zhaoyi Li, Honghao Fu, Takuya Isogawa, Caio Silva, Isaac Chuang
papers.what_it_establishes: Per the arXiv API listing: an optimal quantum purity amplification protocol with experimental validation on superconducting quantum processors, aimed at NISQ noise.
papers.overlap_reason: Concerns increasing the purity of a state (a mitigation/distillation primitive), not estimating purity and not comparing measurement strategies. Included only to record that it surfaced in the purity-on-superconducting-hardware sweep and was ruled out. arXiv API listing only; abstract not fetched.

papers.title: Rigetti Announces General Availability of 108-Qubit System (Cepheus-1-108Q specification)
papers.authors: Rigetti Computing, Inc. (corporate press release, filed with the SEC and mirrored by Quantum Computing Report)
papers.what_it_establishes: NOT prior art but the load-bearing source for the material's central claim, and I verified it independently. The published specification gives: 108 qubits as twelve interconnected 9-qubit chiplets; 99.1% median two-qubit gate fidelity; 99.9% median single-qubit fidelity; ~60 ns gate speed; a 99.9%-at-28-ns CZ prototype benchmark; a stated target of 99.5% median two-qubit fidelity later in 2026; availability via Rigetti QCS and Amazon Braket. NO READOUT OR MEASUREMENT FIDELITY FIGURE APPEARS ANYWHERE. The only readout-adjacent statement is qualitative: upgraded control electronics 'intended to provide a higher signal-to-noise ratio for qubit readout,' with no number attached. I confirmed this omission on the Quantum Computing Report page listing every quoted specification; the investor-relations page itself timed out on fetch, so the confirmation rests on the mirror plus the search-result summaries of the release, which agree on every figure.
papers.overlap_reason: Source document rather than competing work. Recorded here because the material's thesis, that 'the input that was wrong is exactly the one the specification does not publish,' depends on this omission being real, and it is: the published Cepheus-1-108Q specification quantifies one- and two-qubit gate fidelity and gate speed and is silent on readout. This also resolves a separate provenance issue for the authors, since these device specifications trace to the Rigetti press release and not to the Open Quantum whitepaper.

papers.title: Comparison of Superconducting NISQ Architectures
papers.authors: Benjamin Rempfer, Kevin Obenland
papers.what_it_establishes: Compares superconducting architectures including Google Sycamore, IBM Heavy-Hex, and Rigetti Aspen and Ankaa, plus a proposed bus next-nearest-neighbour design, evaluated with QAOA/QUBO benchmarks and compilation tooling.
papers.overlap_reason: The only arXiv hit I found naming a Rigetti Ankaa-generation architecture. It is an architecture/compilation study, not a hardware measurement campaign, and reports nothing about readout, drift or reproducibility. Listed to record that the Rigetti Ankaa/Cepheus device family is essentially uncharacterized in the open literature, which cuts both ways for the material: little competing prior art, but also no independent baseline against which its numbers can be checked.

papers.title: TuniQ: Autotuning Compilation Passes for Quantum Workloads at Scale for Effectiveness and Efficiency
papers.authors: M. A. Hasanat, Jason Ludmir, Tirthak Patel, Rohan Basu Roy
papers.what_it_establishes: Reinforcement-learning selection of Qiskit compilation passes adapted to circuit, backend and current noise profile, improving fidelity and compile time on IBM Quantum Cloud processors.
papers.overlap_reason: Reported because it is one of only three papers citing the seed, so the forward-citation check is complete and its result is negative. A compiler-autotuning paper: no device characterization, no readout, no stability measurement, no purity, no pre-registration. Same research group as the seed.

papers.title: Three Birds with One Stone: Improving Performance, Convergence, and System Throughput with NEST
papers.authors: Yuqian Huo, David Quiroga, Anastasios Kyrillidis, Tirthak Patel
papers.venue_year: Proc. ACM Meas. Anal. Comput. Syst. (POMACS) 2025; arXiv:2510.09578
papers.what_it_establishes: Varies the qubit fidelity map across a VQA's execution to improve result quality, speed convergence, and co-locate multiple VQAs for higher system throughput.
papers.overlap_reason: Second of the seed's three citers; reported to close out the forward search. A VQA scheduling/throughput technique from the same group -- no readout characterization, no stability measurement, no purity, no pre-registration.

papers.title: Computer Science Challenges in Quantum Computing: Early Fault-Tolerance and Beyond
papers.authors: Jens Palsberg, Jason Cong, Yufei Ding, Bill Fefferman, Moinuddin Qureshi, Gokul Subramanian Ravi, Kaitlin N. Smith, Hanrui Wang, Xiaodi Wu, Henry Yuen
papers.what_it_establishes: Community roadmap arguing that early fault-tolerant quantum computing shifts primary bottlenecks from device physics to computer-science-driven system design, integration and EVALUATION, organized around algorithms, error correction, software and architecture.
papers.overlap_reason: Third and last of the seed's citers. A high-level agenda document with no measurements; its call for better evaluation methodology is thin support for the material's framing, but it establishes nothing the material claims. I confirmed only that 'evaluation' is named as a focus area -- the fetched page did not elaborate on benchmarking standards or reproducibility protocols.

papers.title: New quantum internet applications via verifiable one-time programs
papers.authors: Lev Stambler
papers.what_it_establishes: Constructs verifiable one-time programs enabling single-round open secure computation, including differentially private statistical aggregation 'without pre-registration'.
papers.overlap_reason: Included only to document a negative search result honestly: this is the ONLY quant-ph arXiv paper matching the phrase 'pre-registration', and it uses the term in an unrelated cryptographic sense (participants enrolling in a protocol), not the methodological sense of locking predictions before an experiment. It is not prior art.

papers.title: DGR: Tackling Drifted and Correlated Noise in Quantum Error Correction via Decoding Graph Re-weighting
papers.authors: Hanrui Wang, Pengyu Liu, Yilian Liu, Jiaqi Gu, Jonathan M. Baker, Frederic T. Chong, Song Han
papers.what_it_establishes: CITES THE SEED. Observes that real-hardware noise DRIFTS away from a decoding graph's initial weights, degrading MWPM logical error rates, and that MWPM mishandles correlated errors. Proposes zero-quantum-overhead edge re-weighting (alignment + correlation re-weighting) estimated from matching statistics across decoding iterations.
papers.overlap_reason: Shares the two premises drift-is-real and errors-are-correlated, but operates entirely inside QEC decoding. No purity measurement, no readout characterization, no reproducibility or provenance claim, no cloud-access question. Listed for completeness of the forward citation hop; it does not constrain the material's claims and probably does not need citing.

papers.title: Correcting non-independent and non-identically distributed errors with surface codes
papers.authors: Konstantin Tiurev, Peter-Jan H. S. Derks, Joschka Roffe, Jens Eisert, Jan-Michael Reiner
papers.what_it_establishes: CITES THE SEED. Studies surface-code performance when the physical error model is neither independent nor identically distributed across the device, i.e. when the standard i.i.d. assumption fails.
papers.overlap_reason: Theory/simulation of QEC under non-i.i.d. noise. Shares only the abstract premise that real devices violate independence assumptions. No hardware measurement, no readout, no purity, no reproducibility angle. Included to document the full forward hop; not prior art for anything in the material.

papers.title: Quantum outage probability for time-varying quantum channels
papers.authors: Josu Etxezarreta Martinez, Patricio Fuentes, Pedro M. Crespo, Javier Garcia-Frias
papers.what_it_establishes: CITED BY THE SEED. Introduces quantum outage probability and quantum hashing outage probability as asymptotically achievable error rates for a code of rate R_Q operating over a time-varying channel, with closed forms for time-varying amplitude damping channels. Frames time-variation as producing a FLATTENING of QEC error-rate curves.
papers.overlap_reason: Information-theoretic capacity analysis under time-varying decoherence. Shares only the premise that device parameters drift. No readout, no purity, no hardware experiment, no reproducibility or provenance content. Documented as part of the backward hop; not prior art for the material.
